note: A communicative progression: introduce one new control point in each unit, then reuse it in unfamiliar speaking and writing. The course teaches choices in context, not isolated rule memorization.

points.title: Build an argument: concession, contrast and qualification
Report claims carefully: indirect speech, passive and impersonal forms
Choose relative forms: qui, que, dont, où, lequel and ce qui/ce dont
Place events in time: imparfait, passé composé, plus-que-parfait and conditional past
Use the subjunctive for stance, doubt, necessity and concession
Express realistic and unreal hypotheses across present and past
Signal cause, result, purpose and condition precisely
Summarize and attribute ideas with reported speech and tense shifts
Use nominalization and impersonal phrasing without making prose vague
Maintain reference with en, y, relative clauses and lexical cohesion
Ask purposeful questions, follow up and repair an information gap politely
Compare sources, paraphrase claims and state a qualified position
Structure an unprepared spoken argument with signposting and self-repair
Edit for agreement, verb government, register, cohesion and task completion
